aria: Animated recap of the Hawks' 107 to 97 home win over the Pistons: Lu Dort's 3-pointer with 8:56 left that turned an 85 to 84 deficit into an 87 to 85 lead during an 18 to 0 fourth-quarter run, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Nickeil Alexander-Walker's 27 points and 6 threes, the top scorers, how the Hawks won, and the next game at Boston.
notes: Box score from the Atlanta Hawks' 107–97 home win over the Detroit Pistons on Sunday, Nov 22, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, checked line by line against the CBS Sports gametracker box score. All 107 Atlanta points and all 97 Detroit points add up from the player lines, and the quarter scores (29–22–23–33 to 26–26–33–12) add up to both totals: Detroit led 52–51 at the half and 85–74 after three (Covers; CBS; Field Level Media; AP). Threes (15 of 50 to 11 of 32), free throws (20 of 23 to 14 of 14), assists (23–30), blocks (3–6), points in the paint (38–42), fast-break points (23–12) and both biggest leads (13 each) are from Covers; offensive rebounds (24–8) are from the CBS box score and match the Roundtable Sports story. Atlanta's bench points (47) are added up from the box score's reserves (Dort, Wiggins, Ejiofor, Kispert). The two box scores differ by one rebound between Ausar Thompson and Daniss Jenkins, so no individual rebound total for either is shown. Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

Atlanta opened the fourth quarter on an 18–0 run that turned 85–74 into 92–85 (AP), part of a 26–6 run that wiped out a 13-point deficit (Field Level Media). Detroit missed its first seven shots of the quarter (The Detroit News) and did not score until Isaiah Joe's 3-pointer with 4:52 left, more than seven minutes in (AP; Detroit Bad Boys). The Hawks won the quarter 33–12 (line score). Lu Dort scored 10 of his 16 in the fourth (Field Level Media). Corey Kispert's 18 was a season high (AP; Field Level Media). Cade Cunningham had 5 points, his first game of the season without double figures, and a season-high 15 assists (AP; box score). Atlanta has won four straight (AP; Field Level Media; AJC); Detroit has lost two straight (Field Level Media). Atlanta was without CJ McCollum (left calf) and Jock Landale; Detroit without Jalen Duren (right hamstring) and Duncan Robinson (left quad) (Field Level Media). The Hawks play at Boston on Friday, Nov 27 at 8:00 PM ET; the Pistons play at Orlando on Tuesday (Ball Exclusives; Basketball-Reference; Roundtable Sports).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Lu Dort's 3-pointer with 8:56 left (Field Level Media: "Dort's 3-pointer put Atlanta ahead 87-85 with 8:56 left"; AJC: Kispert's 3 cut the deficit to one, "then Dort made a 3 to give them a two-point lead with just over eight minutes to play"). The board's Pistons +1 to Hawks +2 is 84–85 to 87–85. The sources don't say who passed or whether it was off the catch or the dribble, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Atlanta Hawks or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Lu Dort's listed 6-foot-4 and 220 pounds with No. 0 (Basketball-Reference), arms scaled to the 6-foot-8.5 wingspan measured at the 2017 Basketball Without Borders Global Camp (DraftExpress). He is drawn in Atlanta's home white with the default figure (no look on the look sheet yet). It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
